LanguageData.CC_Settings_Post: The post: letters travel with someone
LanguageData.CC_Settings_Post_Tip: Letters written wait in a mailbag at the gate (a spot you place; without one, by the gate) until someone going their way takes them: the post rider, a trade caravan, visitors and guests leaving, a camp breaking up, pilgrims and travellers passing, a people's messengers, the colony's own caravan setting out. One of them walks to the mailbag for the letters on their way, and the letter is read once it gets there. A regular post comes by the colony's age: none for a tribe, a post rider on the road every week or two in the medieval age, a mail run every few days in the industrial, shuttles in the spacer. You can also send a letter with your own rider, who rides out to the town and brings the answer back. Mail for the colony comes the same way: whoever comes in sets it down at the mailbag, and a messenger is sent only when nobody has come for longer than is reasonable. Reach is the time on the road over the land: within the colony's range anyone going that way reaches them, further off only a relay through a nearer town, and some towns are out of reach until radio. A tribal colony gives spoken messages to the carrier instead of writing. Off, a messenger of their people comes to the gate for each letter, as before.

LanguageData.CC_LetterDlg_PostNote: The writer sits down at a table for about an hour to write it, then takes it to the mailbag at the gate, where it waits until someone going that way takes it. The answer comes back the same way.
LanguageData.CC_LetterDlg_SpokenNote: A tribe sends no letters: when someone going that way comes for it, a colonist gives them the words at the gate, and they carry them. The answer comes back the same way.
LanguageData.CC_LetterDlg_RiderNote: {PAWN} takes it from the mailbag once it is written and rides out to them, then brings the answer home. They are away for the whole road there and back.
